units.en: The ⟦0⟧ is a Chinese warlord state in northwestern China with a population of ⟦1⟧. It borders ⟦2⟧ to the southeast, ⟦3⟧ to the south, and ⟦4⟧ to the west. It is the only one of the many warlord nations that starts as a releasable and with a unique focus tree that shares with other warlords and in particular with fellow Ma warlord nations. It may be released and playable by event when, as ⟦5⟧, the player selects the focus March into Khotan.

The Kumul Khanate was a semi-autonomous feudal Turco-Mongol khanate (roughly equivalent to a banner in Mongolia and Manchuria) that existed within the ⟦0⟧ and, after its collapse in 1911-1912, the ⟦1⟧ until it was dissolved in 1930 and replaced with three provincial administrative districts; Hami, Yihe and Yimu. Its former territory is now part of the Hami prefecture in Xinjiang in China.
The khans of Kumul, with Maqsud Shah and his son Nasir Shah being the last ones, ⟦0⟧ of the Mongol Empire some 700 years earlier.
were direct descendants of the khans of the Chagatai Khanate and thus, some 30 generations removed, the last known descendants of the great conqueror Genghis Khan

Maqsud Shah (known to the Chinese as the Hami Wang, to his subjects as Khan Maqsud or Sultan Maqsud and to the Europeans as the King of the Gobi), was a devout muslim ruling over a petty oasis kingdom from an ancient and ramshackle palace in Hami, one of three towns making up the capital of Kumul proper, known to the Chinese as Huicheng. He had a bodyguard consisting of 40 Chinese soldiers armed with Type 88 and Type 24 Mauser rifles and had a Chinese garrisson billeted in the fortified town as well as a Uyghur militia throughout the countryside. The third town in his domain was the New City or Xincheng. By 1928, it was estimated that Maqsud Shah ruled over some 25.000-30.000 Kumuliks, a far cry from the tens of millions once ruled over by his Mongol ancestors. He was responsible for levying taxes, dispensing justice and so forth, through an administration consisting of 21 Begs or local governors.

Throughout Maqsud's reign, Kumul remained relatively peaceful and prosperous. He paid a small annual tribute to Urumqi and in return the Xinjiang government paid him a formal subsidy of 1200 silver taels every year. For the Uyghurs of Kumul, they were free from the typical persecution under Chinese officials. The only tax paid by citizens of Kumul was in livestock, generally sheep or goats, given annually to the Khan. The soil of the oasis was rich and well cultivated. In March of 1930, Maqsud Shah died of old age. His eldest son Nasir Shah should have inherited the throne of Kumul, but the governor of Xinjiang at the time, Jin Shuren, who was quite corrupt, blocked this and dissolved the khanate to seize its revenue for himself and his government, splitting it into three provincial administrations (Hami, Yihu and Yiwu). Yulbars Khan, Maqsud Shah's former court chancellor, was sent to Kumul to set up a local government. The dissolution of the khanate caused uproar among the Kumulik population, as not only would their tax exemption be abolished, but they were now expected to pay one year of back-taxes and Han settlers (including refugees from Gansu ( ⟦0⟧) and Qinghai ( ⟦1⟧) further west) were encouraged to settle in Kumul in vast numbers. This very quickly boiled over and the Kumul area erupted into open rebellion in 1931-1934, during which Yulbars Khan (who may have masterminded the uprising) assisted Nasir Shah in an attempt to restore the khanate and regain his throne, but this was unsuccessful despite inflicting serious losses on the local garrisons, although Yulbars did succeed in ultimately causing the downfall of Jin Shuren. The subsequent fate of Nasir Shah, the heir to Maqsud Shah and the last known descendant of Genghis Khan, is unknown beyond this point.

After Jin Shuren was later ousted by ⟦0⟧ in 1934, Yulbars Khan would later be appointed as Chief of the Procurement Department of the New 36th Division commanded by Ma Hushan ( ⟦1⟧) and as Commissioner for Reconstruction Affairs by the Xinjiang provincial government. After the Islamic rebellion of 1937, where Ma Hushan led the 6th Uyghur Division and the 36th Tungan Division in an assault on Urumchi, was violently suppressed by Sheng Shicai with ⟦2⟧ support (including 5000 intervention troops, airplanes and BT-7 tanks), Yulbars fled to Nanjing and only returned to Kumul in 1946.

Yulbars Khan later led the Chinese Hui Muslim cavalry and White Russian exile forces against the ⟦0⟧ that was invading Xinjiang in 1949, but suffered a defeat and fled to India in 1951, after which he made his way to Taiwan, the home of the exiled Kuomintang Nationalist government. He was appointed Governor of Xinjiang (in absentia) and after publishing his memoirs in 1969, he remained in Taiwan until his death in 1971.

The ⟦0⟧ uses the shared Warlords national focus tree along with the other warlords and may inherit the ⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧ Chinese focus trees. With the ⟦3⟧ expansion enabled, the Warlords national focus tree is expanded, along with a small unique branch only available to the Kumul Khanate. It also grants access to the new shared ⟦4⟧ and ⟦5⟧ focus trees for the warlords at the end of the tree.
The Kumul Khanate national focus tree can be divided into 2 branches and 3 sub-branches and 1 country specific branch:
This branch begins the political focuses for the Warlords.
This branch allows the Warlords to side with ⟦0⟧. This will replace the current focus tree with the ⟦1⟧.

This branch allows the Warlords to side with ⟦0⟧ and be able to replace and annex them with ⟦1⟧ Support. When replacing the ⟦2⟧, The current focus tree will change into the ⟦3⟧ and all Their national spirits will be yours.

This branch allows the Warlords to instigate ⟦0⟧ with the other Chinas, side with the Japanese and then proclaim a rival government different to ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ and give either the ⟦3⟧ or ⟦4⟧ depending on party popularity.
This is the Industrial branch of the focus tree.
This branch modifies the national spirit ⟦0⟧, and either give bonuses to the country's cavalry or mountaineers.

This branch is exclusive to the releasable nation ⟦0⟧. This cores the Sinkiang region, then cores the territory belonging to Ma Cliques and the Muslim regions of China. It will also allow the formation of ⟦1⟧.

The Kumul Khanate can form the ⟦0⟧ (a unique version of the ⟦1⟧ exclusive to Kumul) by progressing down its Warlord national focus tree, completing either the Power Struggle or Proclaim Rival Government national focuses to switch over to the ⟦2⟧ and then completing the ⟦3⟧ national focus and progressing down the subsequent focuses.
Nationalist Chinese Warlord national focus tree

Additionally, the Kumul Khanate can also form ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ through decisions if it can conquer the required territories, most of which are held by ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧ the ⟦4⟧, the ⟦5⟧ and ⟦6⟧ at the start of the game.

No other Chinese nation, warlord or otherwise, is able to form all of these three nations at once, meaning the Kumul Khanate can potentially reach the highest possible core population of any Chinese nation.

Successfully forming all three of these nations will allow the Kumul Khanate to succeed in restoring much of the empire that Genghis Khan, the distant ancestor of the khans of Kumul (themselves the last known descendants of Genghis Khan) once forged seven centuries before the events of Hearts of Iron 4.
